topic: Earth in the Solar System & Its Motions

items.front: Origin of the solar system — hypothesis, age, Sun's share?
items.back: Nebular Hypothesis (Kant-Laplace); ~4.6 billion years ago; Sun took ~99.9% of the nebula's matter.
items.examPoint: Origin of the solar system — Nebular hypothesis (Kant–Laplace), Big Bang, planetesimal; formation ~4.6 billion years ago
items.source: APPSC GK — Solar System

items.front: Terrestrial vs Jovian planets?
items.back: Inner (Mercury-Venus-Earth-Mars): small, rocky, dense. Outer (Jupiter-Saturn-Uranus-Neptune): large, gaseous, many moons. Asteroid belt between.
items.examPoint: Inner/terrestrial vs outer/Jovian (gas & ice giant) planets
items.source: APPSC GK — Solar System

items.front: Which planet is hottest, spins retrograde, and has a day longer than its year?
items.back: Venus (runaway greenhouse; 243-day 'day' vs 225-day year).
items.examPoint: Distinctive planet facts (Venus hottest & retrograde, Mercury temperature extremes, Jupiter largest, Neptune fastest winds, Uranus tilted axis)
items.source: APPSC GK — Solar System

items.front: IAU: the one criterion a dwarf planet FAILS, and the five recognised?
items.back: Has not cleared its orbit. Five: Ceres, Pluto, Eris, Haumea, Makemake (Charon is a moon).
items.examPoint: IAU dwarf planets — Ceres, Pluto, Eris, Haumea, Makemake (Charon is a moon)
items.source: IAU

items.front: Meteoroid vs meteor vs meteorite?
items.back: Meteoroid = rock in space; meteor = streak burning in the atmosphere; meteorite = survives to the ground.
items.examPoint: Comets, and meteoroid vs meteor vs meteorite
items.source: APPSC GK — Solar System

items.front: Sun — composition, mass share, light-travel time; are sunspots hot or cool?
items.back: ~75% H, ~24% He; ~99.86% of the solar system's mass; light takes 8 min 20 s; sunspots are cooler (darker).
items.examPoint: The Sun — structure, composition and solar activity (sunspots, solar wind, flares)
items.source: APPSC GK — Solar System

items.front: Solar vs lunar eclipse — which moon phase, and the shadow terms?
items.back: Solar = new moon (Moon between Sun & Earth); Lunar = full moon. Umbra=total, penumbra=partial, antumbra=annular ring.
items.examPoint: Eclipses — solar & lunar geometry; umbra, penumbra, antumbra; Saros cycle
items.source: APPSC GK — Solar System

items.front: Why aren't there eclipses every month?
items.back: The Moon's orbit is tilted ~5° to the ecliptic; eclipses need a new/full moon near a node.
items.examPoint: Solar & lunar eclipse conditions — new/full moon, nodes, Moon's 5° orbital tilt; umbra
items.source: APPSC GK — Solar System

items.front: Earth's axis is 66½° to the orbital plane — that equals what tilt from vertical, and what does it cause?
items.back: 23½° from the vertical; causes the seasons and fixes the Tropics (23½°) and polar circles (66½°).
items.examPoint: Earth's rotation — period (23h56m/24h), axis tilt 66½°, day & night, circle of illumination, Coriolis effect
items.source: APPSC GK — Motions of the Earth

items.front: Solstice and equinox dates, and what happens on each?
items.back: 21 Jun (Sun over Cancer, longest NH day), 22 Dec (over Capricorn); 21 Mar & 23 Sep equinoxes (Sun over Equator, day=night).
items.examPoint: Axis tilt 23.5° and seasons — solstices (21 Jun/22 Dec) and equinoxes (21 Mar/23 Sep)
items.source: APPSC GK — Motions of the Earth

items.front: What actually causes the seasons (and the July proof)?
items.back: The 23½° axial tilt, NOT Earth-Sun distance — Earth is at aphelion (farthest) in early July, yet the NH has summer.
items.examPoint: Seasons caused by axial tilt, not Earth–Sun distance; aphelion in July
items.source: APPSC GK — Motions of the Earth

items.front: Longitude-time rule and IST basis?
items.back: Earth turns 15°/hour, so 1° = 4 minutes; places east are ahead. IST = 82½°E = GMT + 5:30.
items.examPoint: Longitude & time — 15°=1 hour, GMT/UTC, IST at 82½°E (+5:30)
items.source: APPSC GK — Latitudes & Longitudes

items.front: Coriolis effect — direction of deflection and where it's zero/max?
items.back: Deflects moving air/objects right in NH, left in SH (Ferrel's Law); zero at the Equator, maximum at the poles.
items.examPoint: Earth's rotation — period (23h56m/24h), axis tilt 66½°, day & night, circle of illumination, Coriolis effect
items.source: APPSC GK — Motions of the Earth

items.front: What does the solar system consist of?
items.back: The Sun and everything bound to it by gravity — 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, comets and meteoroids.
